topic: Smart Pointers for Automatic Memory Management
explanation: Smart pointers in C++ are template classes that manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation when objects go out of scope. They are used to prevent memory leaks and dangling pointers, promoting safer and more maintainable code by adhering to RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) principles. Modern C++ encourages replacing raw pointers with smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr for resource management.
code_example: auto ptr = std::make_unique<ClassA>(); // Create a unique_ptr managing ClassA object
ptr->doSomething(); // Use the object via smart pointer
// No need to delete; object is automatically destroyed when ptr goes out of scope
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::unique_ptr to manage a dynamically allocated ClassA object. The smart pointer automatically handles deallocation when it goes out of scope at the end of main(), preventing memory leaks. It also shows modern C++ idioms like std::make_unique for safe and efficient object creation, illustrating how smart pointers promote resource safety and cleaner code.
